Mr. Probir Neogi, Advocate, For the petitioners.
Mr. Khandaker Aminul Haque, Advocate, For the opposite party
parties:
KHANDAKER ANISUR RAHMAN BEING DEAD HIS LEGAL HEIRS: 1(KA) REBEKA SULTANA AND OTHERS
Vs.
BEGUM @ REVA
full_judgment:
Soumendra Sarker, J: The Rule issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 05.05.2004 passed by the learned District Judge, Mymensingh in Civil Revision No.18 of 2004 rejecting the said revisional application summarily and refusing to stay all further proceedings of Other Class Execution Case No. 08 of 2002 should not be set-aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 3. The contrary case of the defendant in short is such that he did not execute the alleged bainapatra dated 23.06.1992 for selling the suit land and only in need of some money on taking a sum of Taka 90,000/= from the plaintiff, he mortgaged the suit property, but the plaintiff subsequently out of ill motive without taking the mortgaged amount instituted the original suit after creating a false bainapatra, for Specific Performance of Contract. 

 4. The Original Other Class Suit No. 52 of 1993 for want of defendant's hazira was decreed ex parte on 15.08.1995. Subsequently, the defendant knowing about the ex parte decree filed a Miscellaneous Case being No. 97 of 1995 for setting aside the same. The said Miscellaneous Case was dismissed on 12.05.1998. Thereafter, the plaintiff instituted the Other Class Execution Case No. 08 of 2002 on 30.11.2002. During pendency of that execution case the Defendant-Judgment-debtor filed an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure on 20.01.2004 for setting aside the execution case on the ground of limitation. The learned Executing Court while rejected that application on 06.04.2004, the Defendant-Judgment debtor being aggrieved filed a Civil Revision being No. 18 of 2004 before the learned District judge, Mymensingh and the learned District Judge by the impugned order dated 05.05.2004 summarily rejected the revisional application. 

 7. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the learned 1st Court of revision as well as the executing Court during passing its judgment and orders committed illegality and irregularity. The learned Advocate further submits that the learned District Judge, Mymensing misdirected himself in grasping the factual aspect of the case, as well as erred in law in deciding the fate of the revisional application. The learned Counsel in his submission argued that on the ground of law point, which is based on the period of limitation for filing of the execution case, the application for setting aside the execution proceedings was filed by the Judgment debtor-Petitioner, but neither the executing court nor the 1st court of revision has been able to appreciate the proposition of law as provided in Article 182 of the Limitation Act. The learned Advocate submits that the decree was passed on 15.08.1995 but the execution case was filed on 30.11.2002, which is apparently time barred as it was filed seven years, three months, fifteen days after the decree. The learned Advocate also submits that under Article 182 of the Limitation Act, 1908 the period of limitation is only 03 (three) years and within this period the execution case shall have to be filed, but apparently the execution case was not filed within that period. The learned Counsel referring a decision of our Apex Court reported in 05 BLC (AD) 07 submits that the Decree holder-Opposite party fraudulently obtained the kabala deed registered through court in the above mentioned execution case, but in fact; the execution of the decree was no longer alive when it was enforced by the alleged execution and registration of the kabala deed through court. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the kabala deed which was obtained through a void execution proceedings is a nullity in the eye of law. 

 8. As against the aforesaid submission of the learned Counsel for the petitioners the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party opposing the Rule submits that the Execution Case being No. 08 of 2002 while was proceeding, there was no order of stay from any higher court and there was no legal embargo in the proceedings of the execution case and accordingly the executing court exhausted all the process of execution and the decree was executed properly by registration of the sub-kabala deed through court in favour of the Defendant-Opposite party. After filing a counter-affidavit, the learned Advocate for the Plaintiff-Opposite party argued that the Other Class Suit No. 52 of 1993 was decreed ex parte on 15.08.1995. Thereafter, the Plaintiff-Decree holder filed Other Class Execution Case No. 08 of 2002. The learned Joint District Judge executed the kabala deed in favour of the Decree holder in pursuance of the order dated 09.07.2009 and accordingly passed necessary order for registration of the said deed. Thereafter on 27.06.2013 the kabala deed being No. 6891 was registered on 02.07.2013 vide Annexure-‘1’. The learned Advocate further submits that the kabala deed was duly executed and registered through court and the entire process of the execution case was lawful and handing over the suit land to the Decree holder was held at the time of execution of the ‘bainapatro’ and thereby the entire process of the execution case has been finalized and confirmed. The learned Advocate lastly submits that, at this stage there is nothing to interfere with the execution proceedings since the cause of action of this civil revision has been ceased by disposal of the execution case. 

 9. In order to appreciate the submission advanced from the side of the learned Counsels for the parties, having gone through the connected papers including the ex parte decree passed by the learned trial court dated 15.08.1995 in Other Class Suit No. 52 of 1993, the application of the Plaintiff-Decree holder dated 10.11.2003 (Annexure-‘D’) for starting the Decree Execution Case, the application filed by the Judgment debtor under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure dated 20.01.2004 for rejection of the Decree Execution Case No. 08 of 2002 (Annexure-‘E’), the order of the executing court dated 22.02.2004 (Annexure-‘F’), the order dated 06.04.2004 of the same court in Execution Case No. 08 of 2002 [Annexure-F (1)], the order of the learned Joint District Judge, of the same proceedings dated 25.04.2004 (Annexure-‘G’), the order dated 11.05.2004 of the executing court (Annexure-‘H’) and the impugned order of the court of revision dated 05.05.2004, it transpires that the original suit for Specific Performance of Contract being No. 52 of 1993 was decreed on 15.08.1995. After that decree, the Defendant-Judgment debtor-Petitioner filed an application for setting aside that ex parte decree under Order IX rule 13 along with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure being Miscellaneous Case No. 97 of 1995. The learned trial court by its judgment and order dated 12.05.1998 disallowed the aforesaid miscellaneous case vide Annexure-‘C’. Thereafter, the Decree holder-Opposite party to this civil revision filed an application for starting the Execution Case on 10.11.2003 vide Annexure-‘D’. It also transpires from the connected papers that the Judgment debtor-Petitioner against the decree execution case stating that the case is time barred filed an application before the executing court on 20.01.2004 to reject the execution proceeding. Subsequently, the learned executing court after different dates on 06.04.2004 rejected that application of the Judgment debtor holding the view that the execution case is not barred by limitation. The Judgment debtor thereafter preferred the 1st Civil Revision being No. 18 of 2004 and filed an application on 25.04.2004 before the executing court supported by an information slip from the court of the learned District Judge, Mymensingh praying for an order of stay of the execution proceedings. The learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Mymensingh without disposal of the said application fixed a date on 11.05.2004 for hearing on that application and deficit stamp papers from the side of the Decree holder. I also find that on the date Fixed i.e. on 11.05.2004 the learned executing court fixed another date on 30.05.2004 for deficit stamp papers for the kabala deed and in the meanwhile the court obtained the order of rejection of the Civil Revision No. 18 of 2004 of the learned District Judge, Mymensingh. 

 10. On meticulous consideration of the papers in connection of the factual aspects of the case, it is evident from the face of the papers that the learned 1st court of revision while passing the impugned order dated 05.05.2004, the execution proceeding was continuing and a date was fixed ahead for depositing the deficit stamp papers. Furthermore, it is noticed that the learned District Judge, Mymensing without going into the legal aspect of the revisional application filed before him in a slipshod manner, by passing the mandatory provision of law as incorporated in Article 182 of the limitation Act, 1908 passed the impugned order dated 05.05.2004 in hasty way, which is imprudent in nature. Obviously, the learned 1st court of revision failed to apply his judicial mind during passing the impugned judgment and order and as such the order itself is not in accordance with law. I also find from the relevant laws that in a execution case for the execution of a decree, the Decree holder has no other alternative but to file the execution case within 03 (three) years from the date of decree. 

 12. Having regard to the decisions referred to from the sides of the respective parties in this instant Civil Rule, I am constrained to hold such a view that our Apex Court's decision is very much clear with regard to filing of the execution proceeding and the period of limitation as prescribed in Article 182 of the Limitation Act (IX of 1908) is 03 (three) years and within this period the Decree holder shall have to file an application for execution of the decree and the court is empowered to proceed with the execution proceedings in that case only. But in the instant case as I have come across from the relevant papers that the executing court was not lawful in the proceedings of the Execution Case No. 08 of 2002, inasmuch as; the said execution case was time barred. Therefore, the subsequent acts of the executing court are not valid in the eye of law. It is crystal clear that the executing court proceeded with the execution proceedings without jurisdiction and as such the sub-kabala deed which was registered through court by the said execution proceeding is void ab initio, which need not be avoided. The kabala deed which was obtained through court by the aforesaid illegal proceedings was obtained fraudently and as such it is a nullity. 

 13. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and order dated 05.05.2004 passed by the learned District Judge, Mymensingh in Civil Revision No.18 of 2004 rejecting the said revisional application summarily and refusing to stay all further proceedings of Other Class Execution Case No. 08 of 2002 is hereby set aside.
